findings.summary: THE STAGED-NAME GUARD -- the one narrowing that makes the escape 'reviewed with the commit it excuses' -- IS BYPASSABLE TWO WAYS, and the new test's own as() message asserts the property that fails. (1) UNESCAPED DOT, the exact defect fixed nine lines below for $TASK and left in place for the filename: `git diff --cached --name-only | grep -qx 'baselines/review.txt'` is a BRE, so any staged path matching it satisfies the guard. MEASURED against a scratch repo built from this diff's own fixture: with `rounds:M9.1  argued for an EARLIER commit` COMMITTED in HEAD and the only staged paths being `docs/...backlog.md` and a file named `baselines/review_txt`, the gate printed `WARN ... ARGUED as 'rounds:M9.1'` + `ok` and exited 0 at round 3. `grep -qxF` closes it. (2) TOUCHED-FILE IS NOT ADDED-LINE: the guard asks whether the FILE is in the staged diff, then reads the whole index blob, so any staged edit to baselines/review.txt re-arms every `rounds:` line already committed for the current task. MEASURED: HEAD carries `rounds:M9.1  argued for an EARLIER commit`; the staged diff adds only `+reviewer:R7  an unrelated finding argued legitimately`; `git diff --cached -- baselines` shows the rounds line as unchanged CONTEXT, and the gate waived the cap at round 3 (exit 0). aROUNDSLineALREADYCOMMITTEDDoesNOTWaiveALATERCap says 'the line must be staged HERE, so each exception is reviewed with the commit it excuses' -- true only while the file is untouched, which is the one case its fixture builds. WHY MINOR AND NOT MAJOR, stated so the call is checkable: both vectors need a `rounds:<this task>` line already in the index, so with baselines/review.txt carrying no rounds: line today neither is reachable, and after the first argued commit each stays scoped to that one already-done task id. It becomes reachable if a task id is argued and then committed under again, or if a rounds: line for a future task is added to this deliberately-growing file ahead of time. FIX, one place, closing both and keeping the index semantics: match the key against the ADDED lines of the staged diff -- `git diff --cached -U0 -- baselines/review.txt | awk '/^[+]/ ...'` -- instead of name-guard plus `git show :`. NIT on the same awk line: `   rounds:M9.1  x` (leading whitespace) now argues the cap, measured exit 0, because awk strips leading blanks -- harmless, except the row and the standard call the record 'greppable' and `grep '^rounds:'` will not find it.
findings.failure_scenario: A task that reaches round three USUALLY also has a finding it wants to argue, so 'the commit stages baselines/review.txt for an unrelated reason' is the normal shape of the population this code serves. Give that task an id that has argued its cap before -- a redone commit, or a rounds: line written ahead of time into a file whose header says a growing list is expected -- and the cap is waived by a line that appears in the diff only as context. The reviewer reading the diff sees `+reviewer:R7`, no rounds: line, and no reason to think a cap was lifted; the WARN that would say so is swallowed by pre-commit (M4.28), so the only surviving trace is `(round 4 of 2)` in a success line nobody sees. That is the escape becoming the workflow the paragraph this diff adds to review.md warns against, arriving invisibly -- and a test whose message says it cannot happen.

findings.summary: THE UNFIXED HALF OF r2-4 IS A COMPLETE CAP BYPASS, not just a `--task '.*'` widening, and it needs no exotic input. `review.sh record` validates --file and --role and NOT --task (`[ -n "$TASK" ]` is checked in the `context` arm only), and nothing ever compares a verdict's task to the commit subject's task. MEASURED, twice, on a scratch repo with four prior rounds on disk: (a) both roles recorded with `--task M9.7` while the prior rounds are M9.1 -> `ok staged bytes reviewed by reviewer test-reviewer (round 1 of 2)`, exit 0, cap silent; (b) both roles recorded with --task OMITTED, which writes `"task": ""` -> rounds_for returns (0, None) and the gate prints `ok ... (round 0 of 2)`, exit 0. Case (b) is worth separating because the gate ASSERTS two verdicts exist for these bytes in the same breath as printing round 0, and this file's own docstring defines a round as a distinct staged hash reviewed for the task -- so round 0 with two verdicts present is a count the definition makes impossible. MY JUDGEMENT ON WHERE IT BELONGS, since the task asked: A ROW, not this commit. The fix is in review.sh, a file this diff does not touch, and it is a real choice rather than a line -- require --task, validate it against backlog.md, or bind it in check-commit-msg.sh, which is the only place the subject's task id and the staged hash are both in scope. But the row has to exist, because 'the cap is a predicate now' -- the claim this diff writes into a standard -- holds only against an honest --task. THE CHEAP HALF IS IN SCOPE: refusing when verdicts exist for $SHA and TASK is empty is one line inside the block this diff rewrote, and it costs nothing to add here.
findings.failure_scenario: An author at round five needs the commit to land. `scripts/review.sh record --file v.json --role reviewer` -- no --task, which is not an error -- twice, and check-reviewed prints ok with `(round 0 of 2)`; pre-commit swallows stdout on success so nobody reads the 0. Both roles are present and no major is unresolved, so every substantive check really did run: the commit looks cleaner than the nine SKIP commits this diff was written to eliminate while defeating the same rule, and it leaves no `SKIP=` in the body for `git log --grep` to find. The measurement that produced the nine would not find it.

findings.summary: r2-5 IS NOT ADDRESSED, AND MY JUDGEMENT IS THAT THE REMEDY TEXT SHOULD SAY IT -- one clause. MEASURED end to end: at round 3 the gate prints `argue it with a STAGED baselines/review.txt line keyed 'rounds:M9.1  <why it cannot be split>'`; doing exactly and only that, the very next run prints `FAIL no 'reviewer' verdict for the staged bytes (438cdbc...)` and `FAIL no 'test-reviewer' verdict ...`, exit 1, with nothing about the cap and no sign the argument was read. Staging the line moves the hash, the earlier verdicts are bound to the old bytes, and the author owes a further recorded round before the escape takes effect. review_rounds.py's docstring now states this plainly ('staging an argument DOES move the hash and DOES cost a round -- which is survivable because the argument is consulted before the count is compared'), so the fact is known in the tree and absent from the one place an author reads it. THIS IS LIVE ON THIS VERY COMMIT: `.harness/review` holds two hashes for M4.21, so recording this verdict makes it three and the cap fires on the diff as staged.
findings.failure_scenario: The author follows the printed instruction, gets a refusal that names verdicts rather than the cap, and concludes the escape does not work -- which is precisely the inference that produced this task's own opening sentence and the nine SKIP commits: 'the argument was written into baselines/review.txt as the message directs, and the gate still refused'. The remedy is now true but incomplete in the same direction as the one it replaced, and the cost of being wrong is another stated skip. `printf` one more line: 'then have both roles record again -- staging the line moves the hash, so it costs one more round.'

findings.summary: THE COUNT r2-3 WAS RAISED ABOUT IS STALE AGAIN, IN THE SAME ROUND THAT FIXED IT. The M4.21 row ends '`review_rounds.py` had NO TEST; it and the cap now have NINE, each falsifiable against its own mutation of the gate -- cap removed, cap at 1, the task ignored in the key, and the worktree read instead of the index'. ReviewRoundCapTest has ELEVEN @Test methods (`grep -c '^  @Test'` = 11), and the four mutations named are the round-1 set: the two the round-2 findings actually bought -- the staged-name guard (aROUNDSLineALREADYCOMMITTEDDoesNOTWaiveALATERCap) and the first-glob-hit task resolution (verdictsDISAGREEINGAboutTheTaskAreREFUSEDRatherThanResolved) -- are the two the sentence omits. Third recurrence in this task by one mechanism: a round's fix adds a test and the count is not extended. The M4.12 row two rows above already draws the conclusion -- 'NO COUNT HERE, deliberately: this sentence said six, then nine, then twelve, and was wrong at every one'. SECOND, SMALLER: the '7 of 12 tasks in one session' figure is now frozen into review.md rule 12 with no command that reproduces it, in the same paragraph that models the right thing for the nine by naming `git log --grep=SKIP=check-reviewed`. It IS measurable from the tree: six lines of python over .harness/review give 21 of 78 tasks over the cap today, M4.12 at 12 and M0.13 at 11 -- which also settles review_rounds.py:5's parenthetical '(five rounds on one, four on two others)' against check-reviewed.sh:37's 'one reaching ELEVEN rounds' in the same diff.
findings.failure_scenario: The row is what `review.sh context` prints to every future reviewer of anything citing M4.21 -- it printed it to me. A reviewer told the suite has nine tests covering four mutations, reading a class of eleven, cannot tell an extra test from a miscount, and the two tests it most needs to know exist are the two the enumeration drops: the next author to simplify the staged-name guard or restore the break-on-first-glob-hit reads the row and concludes neither is pinned. The 7-of-12 half fails later and quieter: it is the calibration for 'a growing list of rounds: entries is a signal', so a reader judging whether the escape is over-used compares against a number nothing in the tree can reproduce, next to one that can.

findings.summary: THE SWALLOW THIS DIFF REMOVED FROM THE GATE IS STILL IN THE PACKET BUILDER, and it is the builder that tells the reviewer which round it is on. review.sh:41 is still `ROUND_N=$(python3 scripts/review_rounds.py "$DIFF_SHA" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)` -- character for character the `|| echo 0` that check-reviewed.sh:46 now refuses to use, and for the reason given there: it cannot tell 'nothing recorded' from 'the records contradict each other'. So the new SystemExit for disagreeing tasks reaches the gate and is hidden from the packet, which prints 'This is round 1 of 2'. Worse and independent of the swallow: rounds_for resolves the task from the verdicts FOR THE CURRENT HASH, and on a fresh round none exist yet, so ROUND_N is 0 and the packet prints 'This is round 1 of 2' on EVERY round. This packet says 'This is round 1 of 2 for M4.21' and '=== THIS IS NOT ROUND ONE ===' with four lines between them, over a diff that is round three. Not introduced here, and out of the staged files -- but this is the commit that makes the round count authoritative and amends the standard that points at it, so a row is owed. review_delta.py already resolves the task the right way: it is passed $TASK from the command line.
findings.failure_scenario: The packet's round line is the only place a reviewer learns that rule 12 is about to bite, and it is the line review.sh's own comment says exists because 'a rule an agent has to RECALL at the deciding moment is the weakest rung'. Every reviewer of every round-two-or-later commit is told it is round one, so nobody applies 'a blocking finding in round two means the commit is too big' -- the reviewer files a blocking finding believing a third round is normal, and the author meets a cap the packet never mentioned. On top of that, a task-disagreement that the gate now stops the commit for is invisible in the packet, so the review is spent before anyone learns the artifacts contradict each other.
